etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English stutten, stoten (“stutter”); cognate with Dutch stotteren (“stutter”).

definitions.definition: (transitive, intransitive) To speak (words) with a spasmodic repetition of vocal sounds.
(intransitive) To expel a gas with difficulty.
A speech disorder characterised by stuttering.

quote.citation: 1626, Francis Bacon, Sylva Sylvarum, London: William Lee, IV. Century, p. 103,[1]
quote.text: And many Stutters (we finde) are very Cholericke Men; Choler Enducing a Drinesse in the Tongue.
